PROGRAM: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
College: College of Arts and Sciences (CAS)
Degree: Bachelor of Science in Psychology (BS Psychology)
Duration: 4 years

Overview: Trains students in the scientific study of behavior and mental processes (developmental, abnormal, social, physiological psychology) alongside research methods and psychological assessment, preparing graduates for further specialization in clinical, industrial/organizational, or counseling psychology.

Skills developed:
- Psychological Assessment
- Psychological Research Methods and Statistics
- Counseling and Helping Relationship Skills
- Clinical Diagnosis and Case Formulation

Career and job outcomes:
- Clinical Psychology Track (Psychometrician / further studies toward licensure): Works as a psychometrician or pursues graduate study and supervised practice toward psychologist licensure under Philippine psychology practice law.
- Human Resources / Industrial-Organizational Psychology Track: Works in human resources, recruitment, training and organizational development roles that draw on the study of workplace behavior.

/ Industrial-Organizational Psychology Track: Works in human resources, recruitment, training and organizational development roles that draw on the study of workplace behavior.
- Counseling / Guidance Track: Works in school or community guidance and counseling support roles, often alongside licensed guidance counselors.

Admission requirement:
- Minimum General Weighted Average (GWA): 88.0

Board/licensure status:
- Board program. Graduates may take the Psychometrician Licensure Examination.

Regulatory basis (CHED): CMO No. 34, s. 2017 - Policies and Standards for Undergraduate Programs in Psychology
Program educational objectives (per this CMO):
- Apply the scientific study of behavior and mental processes to understand individuals and groups across diverse settings.
- Conduct psychological research and assessment ethically, and pursue further training or licensure (e.g. as a psychometrician) as warranted.

the biological bases of behavior, including brain structure, neurotransmission, and the nervous system. Students learn how physiological processes underlie cognition and emotion. This course draws on the biology and chemistry foundation from earlier science electives.
PSY 6 — Abnormal Psychology
CAS | Year 3, Sem 1 | Units: 3 | Prerequisite: PSY (incomplete in source) Studies psychological disorders, their classification, causes, and treatment approaches. Students learn diagnostic criteria and explore case studies of various mental health conditions. This course builds on personality theory and developmental psychology foundations.
PSY 7 — Research in Psychology 1
CAS | Year 3, Sem 1 | Units: 3 | Prerequisite: PSY (incomplete in source) Guides students through the early stages of designing a formal psychological research study. Students develop a research proposal grounded in prior coursework on methodology and statistics. This course is the first half of a two-part research sequence.
PSY 8 — Sikolohiyang Filipino
CAS | Year 3, Sem 1 | Units: 3 Examines psychology through an indigenous Filipino lens, exploring culturally-specific psychological concepts and frameworks.

Foreign Language
CAS | Year 3, Sem 2 | Units: 3 | Prerequisite: FL 1 Builds on basic foreign language skills with more advanced grammar, vocabulary, and conversational practice. Students engage in more complex reading and communication tasks. This course completes the two-part foreign language requirement.
PRACTICUM 1 — Clinical Setting
CAS | Year 3, Inter-Semester | Units: 3 | Prerequisite: PSY courses (incomplete in source) Places students in a supervised clinical setting to apply psychological theory and assessment skills in practice. Students gain direct exposure to real client interactions under professional supervision. This practicum bridges classroom learning with hands-on clinical experience.
PSY 11 — Cognitive Psychology
CAS | Year 4, Sem 1 | Units: 3 Examines mental processes including perception, memory, language, and problem-solving. Students learn cognitive models and how they explain everyday thinking and decision-making. This course adds a cognitive science dimension to the psychology curriculum.
